label: Grinding on
summary: The world holds at 42: no fresh catastrophe, but every open front hardened a notch. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned that any state joining Washington's sanctions will be treated as an enemy, ahead of the promised US 'economic D-Day'. Canada answered Trump's 50 percent tariffs, in force since midnight, with dollar-for-dollar duties on US steel, dairy and electronics from 8 September, and Brent closed a second weekly gain near $94. Ukraine and Russia kept trading deep strikes on each other's logistics. The RSF's encirclement of El Obeid pushed thousands more out of Kordofan, and UN experts warned of mass atrocities. Against that: the first Ebola vaccine doses landed in Kinshasa, Brazilian satellite data put Amazon deforestation at a 13-year low, and solar telemedicine kiosks widened rural care in Chad. No editorial adjustment.
